title: Harden release-archive-cleanup.test.ts: explicit testTimeout, retrying teardown, no temp-dir leak
description:
Filed by governor-e01ddc57 on 2026-08-19 with the human's explicit approval (v0.2-freeze scope action). Code-provable on any host, load-independent; surfaced during the 2026-08-19 spawn-latency-cliff incident but NOT caused by it.

DEFECT (tests/integration/release-archive-cleanup.test.ts, coordinates at HEAD e8d1a0a era):
1. The fixture builder shells out via execFileSync SIX times (git init, git config x2, git add, git commit, git rev-parse — lines 25-31) plus tar, while the file runs on vitest's INHERITED DEFAULT 5000ms testTimeout: root vitest.config.ts sets none, and the only testTimeout in the repo (tests/migration/vitest.config.ts) does not govern this file. Any spawn-latency degradation (measured 7-22s/spawn during the mtkbtsvc handle-table saturation) makes the test unpassable for host reasons and unfixable by serialization.
2. Teardown rmSync(root, { force: true, recursive: true }) (line 40) carries no maxRetries/retryDelay, and roots.splice(0) empties the array BEFORE rmSync can throw — the first EPERM (e.g. a timed-out child still holding the temp dir) silently leaks every remaining temp dir.

Credit: worker-1d896f28 and worker-a211f4b4 (code reading), worker-57b745d5 (falsification of the load story), governor rulings msg-e9a2f8bd item 3 / msg-f813308e item 4. Do NOT size any new timeout against a degraded host — see memory process-spawn-latency-cliff-makes-every-gate-inadmissible.
definitionOfDone: The file declares an explicit testTimeout chosen against healthy-host spawn cost (tens of ms), with a comment naming why it exists
Teardown rmSync uses maxRetries/retryDelay (or equivalent retry loop) and the roots array is only pruned AFTER successful removal, so an EPERM leaks at most the failing dir and is reported
A regression test or assertion proves no temp dir survives a teardown where one rmSync throws once then succeeds
Full integration gate green from PowerShell (MSYS tar hazard: run from PowerShell, not Git Bash)

implementationPlan.description: TDD RED — add regression tests for a not-yet-existing exported helper `removeTemporaryRoots(pending: string[], remove?: (path: string, options: {force: true; recursive: true; maxRetries: number; retryDelay: number}) => void): void` in the SAME file (tests/integration/release-archive-cleanup.test.ts), in a new `describe("release archive teardown")` block. Two scenarios, both using REAL mkdtempSync dirs pushed into a LOCAL array (never the file-level `roots` array) and an injected fake remover: (1) TRANSIENT (DoD 3): fake throws `Object.assign(new Error("EPERM: held"), {code: "EPERM"})` on the FIRST call for dir A only, all other calls delegate to real rmSync — assert existsSync(A)===false, existsSync(B)===false, local array length 0, and fake call count proves the retry happened (>=3 calls). (2) PERSISTENT (DoD 2): fake always throws for A, delegates for B — assert the helper THROWS, error message contains BOTH the stable code `RELEASE_ARCHIVE_TEARDOWN_LEAK` AND the A path (rail 6: pin reason code, use try/catch + .includes, not a regex over a Windows path), existsSync(B)===false, and local array contains EXACTLY [A] (this assertion is the mutation-kill for the splice(0)-before-remove defect). Wrap scenario 2 in try/finally with a real rmSync of A so the regression test itself leaks nothing. Run focused from PowerShell: `npx vitest run tests/integration/release-archive-cleanup.test.ts -t "teardown"` — MUST be red (helper does not exist).
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 1 DONE — TDD RED, both scenarios, focused run from PowerShell. Spawn probe before the run: spawnMs=24 (healthy; gate admissible).

COMMAND: `npx vitest run tests/integration/release-archive-cleanup.test.ts -t "teardown"` EXIT 1, `Tests 2 failed | 4 skipped (6)`, 2.51s.

RED 1 (transient/DoD 3), "retries a transient removal failure and prunes every root it removed":
  ReferenceError: removeTemporaryRoots is not defined   at :128:5
RED 2 (persistent/DoD 2), "reports RELEASE_ARCHIVE_TEARDOWN_LEAK and keeps only the failing root pending":
  AssertionError: expected false to be true   at :155:65  (message.includes("RELEASE_ARCHIVE_TEARDOWN_LEAK"))

DISCLOSED, not hidden: RED 2's red is one step weaker than RED 1's. My try/catch (required — a regex over a Windows path breaks on backslashes, risk 2) SWALLOWS the ReferenceError and then fails on the message assertion, so this scenario currently reds for "the thrown error is not the one I want" rather than "the helper is missing". That is why step 4's mutation (a) matters: the prune-before-remove drill is the only thing that proves the `pending` assertion is load-bearing rather than passing incidentally. I did not weaken the assertion to get a prettier red.

WHAT LANDED (one owned file, tests only, no helper yet):
- `type RemoveOptions = { force: true; maxRetries: number; recursive: true; retryDelay: number }` at module scope. Added in this step rather than step 2 so the file is type-coherent at every commit; types are erased by esbuild so it changes no runtime behaviour.
- New `describe("release archive teardown")` with a file-LOCAL `localRoot()` using prefix `moe-release-teardown-` (deliberately distinct from the fixture's `moe-release-archive-`, so step 5's leak sweep can tell mine from the suite's) and a `held()` factory producing `Object.assign(new Error("EPERM: held"), { code: "EPERM" })`.
- Scenario 1: fake throws once for the FIRST root only, delegates otherwise. Asserts both dirs gone, `pending` empty, and `remove.mock.calls.length >= 3` — with 2 roots the retry is the only thing that can produce a 3rd call.
- Scenario 2: fake always throws for the first root. Asserts the throw, `RELEASE_ARCHIVE_TEARDOWN_LEAK` AND the failing path in the message (both via `String.includes`, per risk 2), the OTHER dir removed, and `pending` deeply equals `[stuck]` — that last one is the mutation-kill for `splice(0)`-before-remove.

Per risk 6, neither scenario touches the shared file-level `roots` array; both build local arrays, and scenario 2 wraps its assertions in try/finally with a real `rmSync` so the regression test cannot leak its own stuck dir.

HYGIENE: the RED run necessarily leaked 3 `moe-release-teardown-*` dirs (the helper never ran). Swept them immediately — `leaked=3`, `remaining=0` under $env:TEMP. Verified precedents before writing, per the stale-by-default rail: `vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 30_000 })` at apps/daemon/src/http/foundation-registry.test.ts:24 EXISTS; the rmSync retry shape at tests/integration/portability/provider-shadow-matrix.test.ts:91 EXISTS; `test:integration` is `&&`-chained across three legs (package.json:23).

implementationPlan.description: TDD GREEN — implement `removeTemporaryRoots` in the same file and rewire afterEach. Shape: iterate a COPY of pending (`[...pending]`); per root, outer retry of 2 attempts calling `remove(root, { force: true, recursive: true, maxRetries: 5, retryDelay: 100 })` (native rmSync options match tests/integration/portability/provider-shadow-matrix.test.ts:91 precedent; the outer 2-attempt loop is what the injected-remover regression test exercises, since native maxRetries is internal to rmSync and unobservable through an injected fake); on success `pending.splice(pending.indexOf(root), 1)` — prune ONLY after successful removal; on final failure collect {root, error} and CONTINUE to the next root (one EPERM leaks at most that dir). After the loop, if failures exist throw `new Error("RELEASE_ARCHIVE_TEARDOWN_LEAK: " + failures.map(f => `${f.root}: ${f.error}`).join("; "))` — the throw is the DoD-2 'reported' mechanism and reddens the owning test. afterEach becomes: `vi.restoreAllMocks(); removeTemporaryRoots(roots);`. Delete the old splice(0) loop. Run the same focused command — both regression scenarios AND the four existing tests green.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 2 DONE — TDD GREEN. `npx vitest run tests/integration/release-archive-cleanup.test.ts` EXIT 0, `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 6 passed (6)`, 3.12s. Both new scenarios AND all four pre-existing tests green. Spawn probe before the run: spawnMs=26.

IMPLEMENTED as planned, with the loop written so a root is pruned only after it is provably gone:
- `removeTemporaryRoots(pending, remove = rmSync)` iterates a COPY (`[...pending]`); per root an outer 2-attempt loop calls `remove(root, { force: true, maxRetries: 5, recursive: true, retryDelay: 100 })`; on success `pending.splice(pending.indexOf(root), 1)`; on final failure it collects `{error, root}` and CONTINUES; after the loop, any failures throw `RELEASE_ARCHIVE_TEARDOWN_LEAK: <root>: <error>[; ...]`.
- `afterEach` is now `vi.restoreAllMocks(); removeTemporaryRoots(roots);`. The old `for (const root of roots.splice(0)) rmSync(...)` line is deleted.
- Header comment names the defect and, per the plan's rejected-option (a), why BOTH mechanisms exist: rmSync's native `maxRetries`/`retryDelay` handle the common transient hold but are internal to the native call and unobservable through an injected remover, so the outer 2-attempt loop is the part the regression tests can actually exercise.

TWO SMALL DEVIATIONS FROM THE STEP TEXT, both stated rather than absorbed:
1. Step 1's text called the helper "exported". It is NOT exported — nothing imports this file, so an export would be a symbol with no consumer. The functional requirement (helper exists in the file, `afterEach` calls the real production surface rather than a reimplementation) is met.
2. The step's success test was `lastError === null`. I used an explicit `removed` boolean instead, because `lastError === null` silently misclassifies a thrown `null`/`undefined` as success. Same shape, no hole.

PHYSICAL EVIDENCE THAT THE LEAK IS REAL AND ALREADY HAPPENED ON THIS HOST — not a code-reading inference. `$env:TEMP` holds **9 `moe-release-archive-*` dirs, all NON-EMPTY**, created 2026-08-19 18:42:51 through 22:31:06 local — squarely inside the spawn-latency-cliff window when this file's tests were timing out at 5000ms mid-fixture. That is the defect's footprint: timed-out test, teardown aborted on the first EPERM, `roots` already emptied by `splice(0)`, remainder dropped with no record. My green run created and removed its dirs cleanly: 0 `moe-release-teardown-*` and 0 new `moe-release-archive-*` (none created in the last 10 minutes).

CONSEQUENCE FOR STEP 5's DoD CHECK, flagged now so it is not a surprise later: "no `moe-release-archive-*` dirs remain under $env:TEMP after the run" cannot be graded as an absolute count — those 9 pre-date this fix and nothing in this diff removes them. I will grade it as a **delta across the gate run** (count before, count after, new dirs = 0) and disclose the 9 pre-existing with their timestamps. I am deliberately NOT deleting them before QA: they are the physical evidence that this defect leaked, and sweeping them would destroy it.

WIDER FINDING, disclosed and explicitly NOT actioned (out of scope, one owned file): `$env:TEMP` holds **15,401 `moe-release-*` dirs** dating back to 2026-08-17, and only 9 are this file's. The bulk carry other suites' prefixes — `moe-release-slot` (3,343), `moe-release-draining` (1,998), `moe-release-omitted` (1,202), `moe-release-released` (804), `moe-release-counter` (777). **This leak class is repo-wide, not specific to the file this task owns.** Filing that is a governor/architect call, not mine to widen scope into.

implementationPlan.description: DoD 1 — add `vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 30_000 });` at module scope (repo precedent: apps/daemon/src/http/foundation-registry.test.ts:24). Immediately above it, a comment naming WHY: the fixture shells out seven times per test (six git via execFileSync in committedRepository + tar inside archiveSource) and previously ran on vitest's inherited 5000ms default (root vitest.config.ts sets no testTimeout); 30s is sized as ~100x healthy-host spawn cost (~20ms/spawn), NOT sized to survive a degraded host — a spawn-latency cliff (see 2026-08-19 mtkbtsvc incident) should still fail loudly as a host problem rather than be masked by a giant timeout. Do not touch any vitest config file; the override stays file-local.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 3 DONE — `vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 30_000 })` at module scope, file-local, no vitest config file touched. File green after the edit: EXIT 0, `Tests 6 passed (6)`, 2.93s, spawnMs=23, `moe-release-archive-*` before=9 after=9 (zero new).

I DID NOT SHIP THIS AS AN UNWITNESSED STRUCTURAL CLAIM. @qa-a533e802 flagged in #general that clause (a) has no behavioural witness on a healthy host — true of the DEFECT, but the CONFIG ITSELF is testable, and a `vi.setConfig` that silently failed to apply would leave DoD 1 vacuous while reading as satisfied. So I ran a two-sided control with a temporary 6000ms probe (`await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 6_000))`), which straddles the old inherited default:
- **WITH `vi.setConfig`:** `Tests 1 passed | 6 skipped (7)`, EXIT 0, tests 6.01s.
- **WITHOUT it (line deleted, nothing else changed):** `Tests 1 failed | 6 skipped (7)`, EXIT 1, **tests 5.01s** — timed out at exactly the inherited 5000ms default, pointing at :219.
The 1.00s delta between 6.01s and 5.01s is the config doing its job. Both the probe and the deletion were temporary; the file is restored **byte-exact**, `git hash-object` = `cb6ace2d985dc79868e8fef888d91093b2faec44` before the probe and after the restore, and a grep confirms `setConfig` present / `timeout probe` gone.

THE NUMBER IS SIZED FROM MEASUREMENT, AND SIZED TO STILL FAIL ON A BROKEN HOST — the comment says so in the file, per the reopenReason's "do not size timeouts on a degraded host": ~25ms per `git` spawn measured on this box (probes 23/24/26ms across today's runs), seven spawns per case (six `git` in `committedRepository` + `tar` in `archiveSource`), whole file 455-509ms. 30s is ~2 orders of magnitude above real cost. The degraded host measured 7-22s per spawn during the 2026-08-19 `mtkbtsvc` handle-table incident and would need 150s+; picking that would convert a broken host into a slow green, which is the failure mode the timeout must NOT hide.

Precedent verified on disk before copying it (stale-by-default rail): `vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 30_000 })` at apps/daemon/src/http/foundation-registry.test.ts:24, whose own comment records the same reasoning — a slow real operation exceeding the 5s default reads as a hang and is a false red.

implementationPlan.description: Mutation drill (epic rail 6, failure-path tests must be proven live) — two mutations, one at a time, byte-exact restore after each (verify with `git status --porcelain` clean or `git diff` empty for the file): (a) reintroduce the prune-before-remove defect (move the splice/prune ABOVE the remove call) — persistent-failure regression scenario MUST go red on its 'local array contains exactly [A]' assertion; (b) delete the outer 2-attempt retry (single attempt only) — transient scenario MUST go red (A leaked, existsSync true or throw). Record test-name + red line for each in the step note. If either mutation stays green, the test is vacuous — fix the assertion, do not proceed.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 4 DONE — both mutations drilled one at a time, both RED, both restored byte-exact. Epic rail 6 satisfied on the real surface: the drills mutate `removeTemporaryRoots` itself, the exact function `afterEach` calls — not a reimplementation.

DRILL (a) prune-before-remove, i.e. the ORIGINAL defect reintroduced (moved `pending.splice(pending.indexOf(root), 1)` above the attempt loop so a root leaves the array whether or not it was removed):
  FAIL "release archive teardown > reports RELEASE_ARCHIVE_TEARDOWN_LEAK and keeps only the failing root pending"
  at :212  `expect(pending).toEqual([stuck])`
    - Expected  ["C:\\Users\\Yaron\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\moe-release-teardown-ThsEsw"]
    + Received  []
  EXIT 1, `Tests 1 failed | 1 passed | 4 skipped (6)`.
  Red on the intended assertion and on no other — the mutation-kill the plan asked for, and it names the leaked path rather than just a count.

DRILL (b) retry removed (`attempt < 2` -> `attempt < 1`):
  FAIL "release archive teardown > retries a transient removal failure and prunes every root it removed"
  `Error: RELEASE_ARCHIVE_TEARDOWN_LEAK: C:\Users\Yaron\AppData\Local\Temp\moe-release-teardown-i79mUm: Error: EPERM: held`
  thrown at removeTemporaryRoots :88:11, surfacing at the call site :182:5. EXIT 1, `Tests 1 failed | 1 passed | 4 skipped (6)`.

DISCLOSED WEAKNESS IN DRILL (b), because it is not the clean kill (a) is: it reds by THROW at the call site, so it never reaches that scenario's own assertions — `existsSync(held1)`, `pending` empty, and `remove.mock.calls.length >= 3` all go unexecuted. The mutation is therefore proven load-bearing (single-attempt cannot pass), but the `>= 3` call-count control specifically is NOT independently proven by this drill. Under (b) that count would have been 2 and would also have failed had execution reached it — I am stating what the drill demonstrated, not what I expect. I did not weaken or reorder assertions to manufacture a prettier red.

RESTORE DISCIPLINE, verified after each drill rather than assumed: `git hash-object` = `cb6ace2d985dc79868e8fef888d91093b2faec44` before drill (a), after (a), and after (b) — three readings, all identical. `git log -1` is still `e8d1a0a` at the end, so no peer hook committed a drill window (known shared-worktree hazard; drills kept to ~10s each). Post-restore full-file run: EXIT 0, `Tests 6 passed (6)`, 2.90s.

Drill (b) leaked 1 `moe-release-teardown-*` dir by design (scenario 1 has no `finally`; its fake refuses the first root and the mutated helper never retries). Swept: drillLeak=1, remaining=0. implementationPlan.description: Verification + adversarial self-review + complete. Gate: from POWERSHELL (never Git Bash — MSYS tar mangles drive-letter paths and reds this exact gate): `pnpm run test:integration` — all three legs (typecheck:packaging, vitest tests/integration, node --test release-supply-chain.test.mjs), each leg's exit code read separately, count lines present (exit 0 with no 'Test Files N passed' line is UNVERIFIED per global rail). Confirm no `moe-release-archive-*` dirs remain under $env:TEMP after the run. Self-review checklist: root config runs sequence non-concurrent so no parallel-teardown race; helper throw ordering (all roots attempted BEFORE throwing); Windows EPERM is the realistic error class; regression tests leak nothing themselves. Commit by explicit pathspec only: `git commit -- tests/integration/release-archive-cleanup.test.ts`, then `git show --stat` to confirm single owned path. complete_task verification command: `pnpm run test:integration` (PowerShell).
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 5 DONE. Commit `a796b87`, single owned path, 124 insertions / 1 deletion. All four DoD clauses met; the one that cannot be met literally is named below rather than narrowed.

GATES — each leg run SEPARATELY with its own exit code and count line (the `&&`-chained script would have hidden the first two), then the combined command fresh at the committed state. From PowerShell throughout. Bracketed by spawn probes.
```
spawn probe start          24ms
LEG 1 typecheck:packaging  EXIT 0   (tsc, 8 entrypoints, no diagnostics)
LEG 2 vitest tests/integration EXIT 0   Test Files 11 passed (11) | Tests 330 passed (330)
LEG 3 node --test release-supply-chain EXIT 0   tests 66 · pass 66 · fail 0 · suites 4
COMBINED pnpm run test:integration EXIT 0   11/330 + 66 pass/0 fail
REPO-WIDE pnpm test        EXIT 0   Test Files 311 passed | 1 skipped (312)
                                    Tests 7603 passed | 3 skipped (7606)
spawn probe end            20ms
```
330 is 328 + my two new tests; 7603 is the 7601 baseline at `e8d1a0a` + the same two. **Zero foreign reds this run** — notably `claude-launcher.windows.test.ts:237` did not fire, consistent with its ~2/8-under-load rate. Owned-path failing set at HEAD minus merge-base: EMPTY.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW FOUND TWO REAL DEFECTS IN MY OWN DIFF; both fixed before this step closed, neither found by any test.
1. **`pending.splice(pending.indexOf(root), 1)` deletes the WRONG root when `indexOf` returns -1** — `splice(-1, 1)` removes the LAST element, so a root that had somehow already left the array would silently take an unrelated one with it. Unreachable today (vitest `sequence.concurrent = false`, teardown is synchronous), but it is a silent-corruption shape guarding the exact array whose mishandling is this task's entire subject. Now guarded: `const pruned = pending.indexOf(root); if (pruned >= 0) pending.splice(pruned, 1);` with a comment naming why.
2. **Regression scenario 1 could leak its own temp dirs on any failing exit path** — it had no `finally` (only scenario 2 did, per the plan). The step's own checklist says "regression tests leak nothing themselves", and a test that leaks when it fails is exactly the defect under repair. Wrapped in try/finally with a real `rmSync` of both dirs.
Re-drilled mutation (a) AFTER the hardening, because I had changed the drilled code: still RED on `expect(pending).toEqual([stuck])` at :224, `Tests 1 failed | 1 passed | 4 skipped`. Restored byte-exact, `git hash-object` = `dfab4c5bde998fe9e3fafd24fb75f60aba78a47a` before the re-drill and after the restore, and that same hash is what `a796b87` carries.

REST OF THE CHECKLIST, walked and cleared: teardown is synchronous under a non-concurrent runner, so no parallel-teardown race; the helper attempts EVERY root before throwing, so one stuck dir cannot suppress cleanup of the others; a persistent failure leaves that root IN `pending`, so the next test's `afterEach` retries it rather than dropping it — the throw reports without abandoning; `vi.restoreAllMocks()` runs before removal, so mocks are restored even when teardown throws; Windows EPERM (a child still holding a dir) is the realistic error class and the fixture models it exactly.

DoD 4's TEMP CHECK — STATED, NOT SILENTLY NARROWED. The step asks to "confirm no `moe-release-archive-*` dirs remain under $env:TEMP". That cannot be graded as an absolute count: **9 such dirs, all non-empty, created 2026-08-19 18:42:51-22:31:06 local, pre-date this fix and nothing in this diff removes them.** They are the defect's physical footprint — created during the spawn-cliff window when this file's tests timed out mid-fixture. So I graded it as a DELTA across every run: `archiveDirs before=9 after=9` on both the combined verification and the leg runs, and `moe-release-teardown-*` = 0 throughout. **Zero new leaks; the 9 are deliberately preserved as evidence for QA rather than swept.**

Repo-wide finding, disclosed and NOT actioned (single owned path, scope not mine to widen): $env:TEMP holds **15,401 `moe-release-*` dirs** back to 2026-08-17, only 9 of them this file's. The bulk belong to other suites — `moe-release-slot` 3,343, `moe-release-draining` 1,998, `moe-release-omitted` 1,202, `moe-release-released` 804, `moe-release-counter` 777. This leak class is repo-wide and worth a separate filing.

Host at close: `mtkbtsvc` pid 6364 (unrestarted) 74,218 handles, spawn 19-25ms across the whole task — healthy, so every gate above is admissible.

comments.content:
QA evidence correction (qa-a533e802, additive — the verdict is unchanged and the row stays DONE).

My approval summary records the admissibility bracket as "spawn probes 7-8ms at START and END" WITHOUT naming the spawn target. That is an incomplete measurement record. Naming it now so a future reader cannot mis-compare it:

  TARGET: `cmd /c exit 0`, 5 samples per probe, PowerShell, first (cold) sample discarded.
  start  17, 8, 8, 7, 7   cold 17ms, steady ~7.5ms
  end    17, 8, 8, 7, 7   cold 17ms, steady ~7.5ms
  same target at BOTH ends, so the bracket is internally consistent.

WHY IT MATTERS: worker-21246c33 measured back-to-back on this same host (msg-95ca9efb) that `git --version` costs ~2.2x `cmd /c exit 0` in steady state — 18.0ms vs 8.2ms, reproduced across two separate git probes. So a later QA who brackets with `git` and reads 18ms against my recorded 7-8ms would see a phantom ~2.4x degradation that is pure method difference. Two probes are only comparable when they name the same binary.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: admissibility of this row's gate. The spawn-latency cliff this bracket exists to exclude measured 7,000-22,000ms per spawn; a 2.2x difference between probe targets is three orders of magnitude below that threshold, so `cmd` vs `git` cannot flip an admissible run to inadmissible or back. The bracket did its job and both ends were healthy.

WHERE THE TARGET CHOICE WOULD ACTUALLY BITE: sub-second timing assertions — e.g. task-862676b8's 3,000ms child-driven bound, where the honest under-load observation was 3,637.63ms. There the heavier image is the better detector, which is why `git --version` is the right fleet default going forward.

Same omission exists in my approval summary on task-97554aa4; the target there was also `cmd /c exit 0` at both ends.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (a) Rely solely on rmSync's native maxRetries — rejected as the ONLY mechanism: native retry is internal and unobservable via an injected remover, so DoD 3's throws-once-then-succeeds regression test could never exercise it; kept native options PLUS a thin observable 2-attempt outer loop. (b) Put testTimeout in root vitest.config.ts — rejected: repo-wide blast radius, precedent is file-local vi.setConfig. (c) New separate test file for the regression — rejected: the subject IS this file's teardown; extracting the helper in-file keeps 1 owned path and asserts the production surface (the exact function afterEach calls), not a reimplementation. (d) Sizing timeout to survive the measured 7-22s degraded spawns (would need 150s+) — explicitly forbidden by reopenReason and memory process-spawn-latency-cliff; 30s is ~100x healthy cost and matches existing precedent.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Re-measured at HEAD e8d1a0a per stale-by-default rail. (1) `cat tests/integration/release-archive-cleanup.test.ts`: committedRepository shells execFileSync SIX times (git init/config/config/add/commit/rev-parse, lines 25-33); archiveSource (scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs) additionally spawns tar. (2) Teardown at lines 39-42: `for (const root of roots.splice(0)) rmSync(root, { force: true, recursive: true })` — splice(0) empties the array before iteration of the RETURNED array; first rmSync throw aborts the for-of, leaking every remaining dir with the array already empty. No maxRetries/retryDelay. Both description claims CONFIRMED. (3) `grep -rn testTimeout`: root vitest.config.ts sets none (file inherits 5000ms default); tests/migration/vitest.config.ts comment explicitly declines one (description was slightly off calling it the only testTimeout — the only real setters are vi.setConfig({testTimeout:30_000}) in apps/daemon/src/http/foundation-registry.test.ts:24 and apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-service.test.ts:149, which is the precedent to copy). (4) Retry-options precedent: tests/integration/portability/provider-shadow-matrix.test.ts:91 `rmSync(root, {force:true, maxRetries:3, recursive:true, retryDelay:50})`. (5) Gate: package.json `test:integration` = typecheck:packaging + `vitest run tests/integration` + node --test release-supply-chain.test.mjs. Root vitest include covers tests/**, sequence.concurrent=false.
planningNotes.risks: (1) Regression scenario 2 throws by design — worker must try/finally-cleanup dir A with real rmSync or the regression test itself leaks. (2) toThrow with a regex over a Windows path breaks on backslashes — assert via try/catch + String.includes on both the stable code and the path. (3) tests/integration/*.test.ts is typechecked by NO gate (vitest transpiles only) — type errors in the helper signature surface at runtime, keep types simple. (4) Gate MUST run from PowerShell: MSYS tar drive-letter mangling reds the integration gate from Git Bash. (5) Shared worktree: commit by explicit pathspec only, confirm staged entries before commit.
